articles.title: El entrenador del Girona explota por una vergonzosa agresión a Iyana Martín: "Está de moda pegarle de h..."
articles.standfirst: Roberto Íñiguez, muy crítico con la agresora Radostina Dimitrova y con los árbitros: "Me cago y me meo si no se puede usar el instant replay".
articles.summary: Roberto Íñiguez, muy crítico con la agresora Radostina Dimitrova y con los árbitros: "Me cago y me meo si no se puede usar el instant replay".
articles.body: Iyana Martín sufrió una agresión en el partido de Eurocup que el Spar Girona disputó este jueves ante el BC Montana 2003 búlgaro. Faltaban 6:28 para el final y las catalanas ganaban por un cómodo 81-57 (acabarían venciendo por 96-71) cuando, aprovechando un bloqueo, Radostina Dimitrova le dio un tremendo codazo en la nuca a propósito a la base española, que se quedó tendida en el parqué con muestras de dolor. Martín tuvo que ser atendida sobre la cancha, se fue al banquillo aturdida y ayudada por miembros del cuerpo técnico del Spar Girona. No volvió a pisar la pista y, después del partido, tuvo que estar en observación después del golpe recibido. Roberto Íñiguez, entrenador del Spar Girona, fue muy crítico en rueda de prensa. "No me puedo callar. No me ha parecido correcto lo que ha pasado con Dimitrova. Creo que ha sido adrede y lo peor ha sido su actitud, riéndose y jaleándose como: 'Ya os he dicho que le iba a dar", dijo el técnico. Al parecer, en el reciente partido de las Ventanas FIBA entre España y Bulgaria ya había habido algún pique entre ambas jugadoras y la búlgara, por lo visto, no se olvidó. "Tenemos a una jugadora que a ver qué pasa. Parece que es el muñeco del pim-pam-pum ahora. Está de moda pegarle de hostias a Iyana", se quejó el entrenador vitoriano, que recibió una técnica por protestar pidiendo más castigo para la agresora, que fue sancionada con una falta flagrante: "No ha sido justo lo que han pitado los árbitros. Deberían haber descalificado a esta jugadora. Hay que jugar duro, pero eso no es jugar duro, eso es de ser una sinvergüenza". Íñiguez cuestionó la labor de los colegiados y el uso del instant replay. "Los tres árbitros me dicen que no pueden verlo porque no hay. Bueno, bien, primero sí hay. Luego, no lo puedes usar en Eurocup, cosa que me cago y me meo, que no se puede usar el instant replay. Si tenemos la máquina y tenemos la instalación y la tecnología, ¿por qué no se usa el instant replay? A ver, que alguien me lo explique. Lo ha visto todo el mundo y tres no lo habéis visto. Pues no lo entiendo", lamentó.

articles.title: Stephen Curry and Cameron Brink's family connection makes Ayesha's bridesmaid role even more special at Stanford wedding
articles.summary: Stephen Curry and his wife Ayesha were at Stanford Memorial Church on Nov. 14 when WNBA star Cameron Brink married her longtime partner, Ben Felter.
articles.body: Stephen Curry and his wife Ayesha were at Stanford Memorial Church on Nov. 14 when WNBA star Cameron Brink married her longtime partner, Ben Felter. Ayesha stood with the bridesmaids, a role with years of shared history behind it. The Golden State Warriors guard and the Sparks player have known each other since childhood, and their families have been close for just as long. Vogue published photos from the day ten days later. The couple celebrated at the Ritz-Carlton in Half Moon Bay with family, friends, and Brink's Sparks teammates.Why does the Curry family connection matter at Cameron Brink's wedding?Stephen Curry and Brink are god-siblings. They have known each other since childhood, and the link runs through both families. Their fathers played together at Virginia Tech. Their mothers were college roommates. Curry's mother, Sonya, is Brink's godmother, and she had a part in the ceremony itself. For Curry, being there meant a lot for that reason.One photo in the Vogue feature shows Sonya praying over the newlyweds. Brink wrote the caption herself: "My wonderful godmother Sonya praying over us."Ayesha's spot among the bridesmaids fits that history. The Currys' daughter, Ryan, was the flower girl and later sang "Until I Found You" during the first dance. Curry and Ayesha also posed for a photo with Brink and Felter during the celebration.The groom had kind words for the pair as well. "Hope to build a family as beautiful as Steph and Ayesha's one day," Felter wrote. The groom named their marriage as the example he wants to follow in his own.Stanford ceremony, Half Moon Bay reception and WNBA reactionsThe couple picked Stanford for the ceremony because it is their alma mater, and it is where they met as students in 2020. The reception moved to the Ritz-Carlton in Half Moon Bay. Guests got an outdoor cocktail hour, speeches, dancing and a cigar lounge, with floral arrangements and greenery throughout the venue. Curry and Ayesha were among several high-profile guests there. The wedding party wore custom outfits, and the newlyweds rode to the reception in a 1957 Rolls-Royce.The ceremony fell on a Saturday. Ten days later, Brink and Felter shared photos with Vogue and sat down for an interview about how they planned the day. John & Joseph Photography took the pictures. The pictures drew quick reactions from the WNBA. Caitlin Clark liked the Instagram post, and Angel Reese left a "gorgggg" in the comments. Nneka Ogwumike, Skylar Diggins, Paige Bueckers and Lexie Hull wrote congratulations as well, along with Olympian Lindsey Vonn. articles.title: Donovan Mitchell gives Jalen Brunson credit for his achievements with the New York Knicks
articles.summary: Donovan Mitchell and Jalen Brunson have played against each other for a long time, but that hasn’t stopped the Cleveland Cavaliers guard from giving the 2026...
articles.body:
Donovan Mitchell and Jalen Brunson have played against each other for a long time, but that hasn't stopped the Cleveland Cavaliers guard from giving the 2026 Finals MVP the praise he deserves.

The two star guards faced off, and once again it was Brunson who came out on top, as the New York Knicks secured a 121-102 win in the NBA Cup game.

Mitchell and James Harden combined for 58 points, but their efforts proved to be in vain, as the Knicks got contributions from everyone in their starting lineup, while Jose Alvarado added 21 points off the bench.

It was another disappointing defeat against the Knicks, a team that swept the Cavaliers in the Eastern Conference Finals on their way to winning an NBA championship.

Although disappointed about the result, Mitchell made sure to heap praise on how Brunson has carried the Knicks since he joined the franchise.

Donovan Mitchell speaks on Jalen Brunson's journey to helping the Knicks win a championship

Brunson and Mitchell were in the same high school class and connected over basketball. Despite the rivalry, Mitchell and Brunson share a great relationship. The Knicks guard was even at Mitchell's wedding in August.

After the game, Mitchell, who was linked with the Knicks before his move to the Cavs, was asked how he felt about Brunson achieving all the success he had with the Knicks.

He said: "Known him since high school. To see his ascension, it's always great to see someone that you know for so long, it s**** it was against us, but at the end of the day man, he is a great human. Works his b*** off and you can see that in the way he finished the season last year. To see the city rally around him, he deserves that; he's worked for it," said Mitchell during the press conference.

"My job is to go out there and to find a way to kill him every time we're out there, but you know, outside of basketball, that's a friend. Got nothing but love for him and his family. I've never seen something like that growing up. A championship here, it hurts that it was against us, but at the end of the day you've got to have nothing but respect."

Even when they met in the playoffs, Brunson heaped praise on Mitchell and his work ethic. This shows that while the NBA is all about competition, respect is at the centre of everything in the league.

articles.title: NBA Europe Arena Investment Plan Gets Wall Street Heavyweights Behind It
articles.summary: The NBA’s push into Europe just got a lot of financial muscle behind it. On Wednesday, the league announced plans to help mobilize at least €10 billion, roug...
articles.body:
The NBA's push into Europe just got a lot of financial muscle behind it. On Wednesday, the league announced plans to help mobilize at least €10 billion, roughly $11 billion, for new and renovated arenas and the entertainment districts around them across Europe. The NBA Europe arena investment initiative is meant to support the league's planned 2027 launch of a new competition with FIBA.

NBA Europe Arena Investment: Who Is Behind the €10 Billion Plan

The league is assembling a group of global investors that includes Apollo Sports Capital, Ares Management, Arctos (a KKR business), Blackstone, HPS Investment Partners, J.P. Morgan, Sixth Street and Stonepeak , among others.

The NBA itself isn't committing to spend the full amount. Instead it's pulling together investors to help finance the projects, and it expects commitments to exceed €10 billion over time as more join. Commissioner Adam Silver called it "a major opportunity" for clubs to build facilities that honor European basketball traditions while improving the fan experience. The investors said in a joint statement they were excited to support the effort.

Projects could go beyond the buildings themselves. Depending on local needs, they could include housing, workplaces, restaurants, retail and public spaces. The league says many major European cities lack arenas with the capacity, hospitality and media infrastructure that are standard in North American sports.

A study by The Sports Consultancy, cited by the NBA, estimates the new league could generate more than €24 billion in gross value added to Europe's GDP over its first decade, and support nearly 15,000 full-time-equivalent jobs a year. One arena has reportedly been designed with a potential London franchise in mind as its anchor.

The initiative is separate from the process of selecting team owners. Franchise cities and owners aren't finalized. Reports describe a structure with 12 permanent franchises and four rotating clubs, targeting a launch in the fall of 2027. The NBA and FIBA first confirmed the project in March 2025.

It also raises the stakes in a financial fight with the EuroLeague, which isn't backing the project . Reports say the EuroLeague committed €3.4 billion to its members over a decade, while the NBA has promised its future teams billions in revenue sharing over its first 10 years.

For now, the NBA Europe arena investment plan is a target, not a done deal. The next milestones are formal investor commitments, announced franchise cities and any settlement with the EuroLeague. But it addresses one of the biggest practical obstacles to a 2027 launch.

Christian Caple brings back the home-and-home concept for On Montlake in a discussion with Oregon writer Tyson Alger. Caple and Alger talk about how UW-Oregon is a meaningful and emotional game, even without major, nationwide implications on the national championship. In this case, there are certainly CFP implications because Oregon can still reach the playoff. Every game is a playoff game for the Ducks at this point, so putting a functional end to their National Championship pursuit for the 119th time would be a great feather in the cap of this UW team.

The Huskies already have a tall mountain to climb as two-TD underdogs against the resurgent Ducks. That mountain would be even more step without the best skill position players on the roster. Both Chris Lawson and Dezmen Roebuck are listed as Questionable for the Huskies on the Wednesday injury report. If either one is missing, it will make Demond Williams' job considerably tougher against a defense that is already going to create plenty of problems.

While UW Men's Basketball leaves the Maui Invitational with a 1-2 record, there were definitely bright spots in the Dawgs' performances. UW lost the 5th place game by a bucket against a solid VCU team. All three teams the Dawgs played in Hawaii were clearly superior to any of the teams on their schedule before the invitational. Even a close loss to ranked BYU and a one-possession defeat against a strong VCU team show that UW can be more competitive than wins over some of the worst teams in the NCAA.

Husky Men's Soccer will get another bite at the apple on Sunday against Big 10 Champion Indiana, this time in the third round of the NCAA tournament. Indiana beat UW just two weeks ago in a penalty shootout to take the Big 10 Tournament. They also beat the Huskies 1-0 in the regular season. If the Dawgs can flip those results, it will send them to the national quarterfinals as they try to repeat as National Champions.

articles.body:
Happy Turkey Day! I am thankful for (you guessed it) Luke Murray. And to add to your turkey, mashed potatoes, and whatever else will appear on your plate tonight, we have some hoops. Boston College heads down to Florida and will face UCF today and Cincinnati tomorrow. Suffice it to say we will learn a lot about this Eagles team in the next 24 hours.

Who: Boston College Eagles (6-0) vs. UCF Knights (4-2)

Where: State Farm Field House, Kissimmee, FL

UCF enters this one having lost two in a row, albeit against Power Four competition. After taking down FGCU, Yale, South Alabama, and GA Southern, the Knights lost by three to Mississippi State and by eight to a ranked Vanderbilt squad.

For the Eagles today, the mission is simple: contain Dior Johnson. The senior guard leads the COUNTRY in points at 29 per game, along with 4.2 boards and 3.5 assists. And his production is not just the result of a high usage rate, either. He's shooting 55% from the floor and 50% from three on over four attempts per game, plus 9.7 free-throw attempts as well. My guess is we will see a heavy dose of Armoni Zeigler pestering him on the ball. Guys like Shelton or Frankel might also see some time picking him up.

Slowing Johnson down is so essential because the Knights only have one other double-digit scorer in Arturo Dean (13.8 points per game) on just 41.7% from the floor. Defensive intensity will be key for the Eagles. UCF also offers a decent matchup in terms of size; UCF only features one seven-footer in its regular rotation (John Bol).

For BC, the obvious question is whether Money Williams plays. If he does not, I'm expecting another big game from Brandon Benjamin and Zak Smrekar to pick up the slack. Ernest Shelton needs to get going. Defensively, it will be very interesting to see how well guys like Smrekar and Colby Duggan defend at the point of attack. Will a Power Four team with UCF's athleticism be able to take advantage of BC's lack of perimeter foot speed?

Should be a fun one this afternoon. Enjoy Thanksgiving, and go Eagles!
